title: VORP — Value Over Replacement (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: VORP (Value Over Replacement Player). SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: How many fantasy points a player is worth ABOVE the freely-available 'replacement' player at his position. HOW TO READ IT: A high VORP means the player gives you an edge a waiver pickup can't; a low VORP means his raw points are nice but everyone has that. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For ranking players ACROSS positions on one board (a 300-point RB and a 300-point WR are not equally valuable) -- it beats raw projected points, which ignore how deep each position runs. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't treat VORP as fixed -- it depends on league size and roster slots; the same player has different VORP in a 10-team vs 14-team league. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Replacement Level (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Replacement Level. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: The baseline points you could get for free at a position -- roughly the last starter who'd be rostered (e.g. about the last starting RB or WR in a standard league). HOW TO READ IT: Everything above this line is real draft value; everything at or below it is replaceable. The line moves with league size and how many of each position start. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: As the anchor under VORP and tiers -- it beats comparing players to zero, because zero points isn't your real alternative; the next man up is. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't set one replacement line for all positions -- QB runs much deeper than RB, so a position's scarcity, not its point total, sets its baseline. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Positional Scarcity (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Positional Scarcity. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: How quickly the talent at a position drops off -- where the cliffs are between the studs and the replaceable crowd. HOW TO READ IT: A steep drop-off means you should pay up early (a few elite, then a desert); a flat position means you can wait. RB has historically been the scarce one, WR deeper. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For deciding WHEN to draft a position, not just who -- it beats taking the highest projected player when a scarcer position is about to fall off a cliff. COMMON MISTAKE: Scarcity shifts year to year and by format -- don't hard-code 'RB is always scarce'; read the current board's actual drop-offs. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Draft Build Archetypes (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Build Archetypes (Hero RB, Zero RB, Robust RB, Late-Round QB, Elite QB Stack, etc.). SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: Named roster-construction strategies -- coherent plans for how to spend early picks across positions. HOW TO READ IT: 'Zero RB' loads up WR early and finds RBs late; 'Robust RB' does the opposite; 'Late-Round QB' waits on QB to stack value elsewhere. Each is a bet about where this year's value lives. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For having a plan that survives the draft's chaos -- it beats best-player-available with no shape, which leaves you thin somewhere. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't marry a build before the draft -- the right one emerges from how the board actually falls; forcing Zero RB when elite RBs slide is leaving value on the table. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Build Affinity (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Build Affinity. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: How well a specific player fits a specific draft build -- a fit score between a player and a strategy. HOW TO READ IT: A high affinity means this player advances the plan (an early-round bell-cow RB fits Robust RB; a high-upside late WR fits Zero RB). Low affinity means he's fine but off-plan. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For turning a strategy into pick-by-pick decisions -- it beats a static ranking that can't tell you whether THIS player serves YOUR build. COMMON MISTAKE: Affinity is relative to a build -- don't read a low score as 'bad player'; he may be elite for a different plan. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Tiers and the Tier Cliff (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Tiers + Tier Cliff. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: Players grouped into bands of similar expected value, and the 'cliff' where the next band drops sharply. HOW TO READ IT: Inside a tier, players are roughly interchangeable -- so you can wait. A cliff approaching means grab one now before the quality falls off. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For draft-day timing -- it beats a flat 1-to-200 ranking, which makes the 14th and 15th player look meaningfully different when they're not. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't chase a marginal in-tier upgrade with an early pick -- spend that pick where a cliff is about to cost you a whole tier. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Scoring Format Effects: PPR vs Standard (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Scoring Format (PPR / 0.5-PPR / Standard). SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: How much each reception is worth, which reshuffles player value. HOW TO READ IT: Full PPR lifts pass-catching backs and high-volume slot receivers; Standard tilts back toward touchdown-and-yardage runners. The same player can move tiers between formats. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For reading a board in YOUR league's scoring -- it beats a one-size ranking that misvalues a reception-heavy player in the wrong format. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't carry a PPR ranking into a Standard league -- the catch-dependent players are overrated there, and vice versa. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: FLEX Value (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: FLEX Value. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: The value of a roster slot that can hold an RB, WR, or TE -- and which position best fills it. HOW TO READ IT: The FLEX raises the replacement bar for whichever position is deepest, because that position's mid-tier players now compete for an extra starting spot. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For valuing depth at flexible positions -- it beats counting only dedicated slots, which undercounts how many RB/WR you actually start. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't fill FLEX by name recognition -- fill it from whichever position gives the best points-above-replacement that week. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: SuperFlex / 2QB Value (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: SuperFlex (a flex slot that can start a QB). SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: How starting a second QB reshapes value -- QBs become far scarcer and shoot up the board. HOW TO READ IT: In SuperFlex, even mid-tier QBs carry premium value because nearly every team wants two; waiting on QB (a single-QB staple) becomes dangerous. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For drafting any league that starts a second QB -- it beats a 1QB board, which badly underrates quarterbacks. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't apply 1QB 'wait on QB' wisdom in SuperFlex -- the position's scarcity flips, and late-QB builds get left behind. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Bye-Week Coverage (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Bye-Week Coverage. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: Whether your roster can field a legal, competitive lineup every week once bye weeks knock players out. HOW TO READ IT: A roster stacked with players sharing the same bye has a hidden hole -- one week where it can't start a full team; good coverage spreads byes across the schedule. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: As a late-draft tiebreaker between similar players -- it beats ignoring byes, which can cost a near-certain loss in one week. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't over-optimize byes early -- it's a minor tiebreaker, not a reason to pass a clearly better player in the first rounds. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Auction vs Snake Draft Value (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Auction vs Snake draft formats. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: How the draft mechanism changes value -- snake gives fixed pick slots; auction gives every player a price and a budget. HOW TO READ IT: Auction lets you buy ANY player if you'll pay, so stars are gettable but expensive; snake locks value to draft position. Value-over-replacement converts cleanly into auction dollars. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For pricing players in auctions -- it beats importing snake rankings, which don't tell you what to PAY. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't spend up for two studs and field replacement everywhere else -- auction punishes a top-heavy roster with a thin bench. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Draft Fit Score (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Draft Fit Score. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: A single pick-time score combining how well a player fits your build with his value over replacement, nudged for positional scarcity and bye fit. HOW TO READ IT: The recommended pick is the one that best advances your plan AND your points -- not merely the highest-ranked name. It generally weighs build fit, value-over-replacement, and scarcity pressure. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: For live draft recommendations -- it beats a static cheat sheet that can't react to your roster's needs as the draft unfolds. COMMON MISTAKE: Don't follow it blindly against obvious context (news, injuries) -- it scores structure, not late-breaking information. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).
